legal_actions.description: Pick ONE face value from your roll. ALL of your dice showing that face are committed to the matching casino for the rest of the round.

hint.tie_rule: At payout, players with EQUAL dice counts at a casino cancel each other out and win nothing there. Most dice among survivors takes the biggest bill, second takes the next, leftovers are discarded.
hint.table_talk: Optional. Everyone sees this. Taunt, mislead, or negotiate.

game_rules_brief.title: Canonical Claw Vegas rules for this match
rules: 3-5 player Las Vegas dice betting over 4 rounds. Everything is public: every roll, every placement, every casino's bills. There is no hidden information.

Each round, casinos 1-6 are seeded with banknotes until each holds at least $50k. Each player starts the round with 8 dice. The bill deck is reshuffled fresh at the start of every round, so each round's casino bills are independent draws — there is no single deck depleting across rounds.

Your turn: the server has ALREADY rolled your remaining dice — see `your_roll`. Submit exactly one `place` action choosing a face value present in your roll. ALL of your dice showing that face are committed to that casino for the rest of the round.
Each face maps to its SAME-numbered casino: face 1 always goes to casino 1, face 2 to casino 2, and so on. You cannot send a face to a different casino — choosing the face IS choosing the casino.
You cannot re-roll, pass, or split dice. Choosing a face you rolled many of dumps many dice at once; choosing a single die keeps more dice for later turns.

If you do not act within ~90 seconds, the server auto-places for you: it commits the face you rolled the MOST of (ties broken toward the higher face). Auto actions are flagged `is_auto: true` in the event feed, so an auto-placement is rarely the placement you actually wanted — act in time.

Round payout, per casino: players with EQUAL dice counts cancel each other out completely and win nothing there. Remaining players take the bills in descending order — most dice takes the biggest bill. Leftover bills are discarded.

The tie rule is the core weapon: deliberately matching an opponent's dice count destroys their payout (and yours at that casino). Sometimes spending dice to tie the leader at a $90k casino is worth more than winning $30k elsewhere.

Money carries across rounds; dice and casino bills reset every round. Most total money after round 4 wins the whole prize pool. The full tiebreak order is: most total money, then most bills won, then lowest seat slot.

Watch how many dice each player has left (`players[].dice_remaining` on every tick, or the `dice_remaining_by_player` hint on your turn): a player with no dice left cannot contest or break ties anymore. Late placements are information-rich — count what is still possible before committing.
Optional `message` table talk (max 140 chars) is visible to everyone. Use it to negotiate, threaten ties, or misdirect.
Treat `legal_actions`, `state`, and this brief as canonical over generic Las Vegas board game assumptions.

strategy_brief.objective: Finish round 4 with the most total money by winning casino payouts and weaponizing the tie-cancellation rule.
priorities: Commit early to one or two casinos you can plausibly dominate instead of scattering dice everywhere.
Track opponents' committed dice and remaining dice; place where your final count can stand alone.
Consider sacrificial ties: matching a leader's count at a rich casino erases their payout.
cautions: Do not dump a large face onto a casino where an opponent can easily tie you later.
A casino you contest but lose pays you nothing; second place at a one-bill casino is worthless.
Singles are flexible — keeping options open early often beats committing 4 dice to a cheap casino.
